reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Hezekiah's and Josiah's matching superlatives as praise for different virtues, trust versus law-keeping, so neither claim is exclusive.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Otto Thenius catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Otto Thenius, Die Bücher der Könige (1849).

sides.snippet: He trusted in Yahweh, the God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor [among them] that were before him.
sides.verseText: He trusted in Yahweh, the God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor [among them] that were before him.

sides.snippet: Like him was there no king before him… neither after him arose there any like him.
sides.verseText: Like him was there no king before him, who turned to Yahweh with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; neither after him arose there any like him.
